paper_metadata.title: Improving strength-ductility synergy of TiNbVTa refractory high-entropy alloys at room temperature by Cr microalloying

evidence.quote: Due to their excellent mechanical performance at elevated temperatures, TiNbVTa-based alloys have emerged as a focal point of research within the field of refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs).

The Cr0 alloy composition features a microstructure comprising a mixture of columnar and equiaxed grains, with an average grain size of approximately 157 μm, as illustrated in Fig. 4 (a – c).
This compositional change also results in a reduction of the average grain size to approximately 143 μm, as depicted in Fig. 4 (d – f).

It is observed that the Cr0.7 RHEA also solidifies into an equiaxed grain structure, with the average grain size increasing to approximately 165 μm, suggesting that excessive Cr addition leads to slight grain coarsening, as shown in Fig. 4 (h – j).

evidence.quote: This phenomenon arises from the locally ordered arrangement of solute atoms in SROs, which generates lattice distortion fields that elastically interact with dislocations, thereby increasing the stress required for dislocation slip

In particular, the contribution of Cr to solid solution strengthening in the Cr0.35 alloy is calculated to be 79.4 MPa.

Notably, microalloying with 0.35 at.% Cr markedly strengthens the alloy, raising the YS by 22.5 % (from 736 ± 24 MPa to 903 ± 22 MPa), the UTS by 19.8 % (from 780 ± 19 MPa to 934 ± 23 MPa), and the El by 7.2 % (from 17.4 ± 3.2 % to 18.7 ± 2.6 %).
